reasons: The take-or-pay commitment 'without reduction or termination rights' is properly within scope of rule LD: it is a Customer-payable minimum amount that survives termination, matching the detection cue 'minimum fees on termination' even though no clause is labelled 'liquidated damages'.

The redline reaches the preferred position (no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum or early-termination charge payable by Customer) and limits payment to Services actually ordered and received; the high changed-character ratio is justified because the rule requires deleting the take-or-pay obligation, which cannot be done with a surgical word change.

The comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, and offers the sanctioned fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees), so it is actionable for negotiation.

Minor drafting tension worth tightening on the next pass: the first sentence preserves 'purchase commitments, if any, ... stated in the applicable Order Form' while the second denies any 'minimum fee', which a counterparty could argue is internally inconsistent; consider clarifying that Order Form commitments remain subject to Customer's termination/reduction rights.
